claims.value: Contract of 25 April 1483 with the Confraternity of the Immaculate Conception
claims.statement: A contract dated 25 April 1483 bound Leonardo and the half brothers Ambrogio and Evangelista de Predis to gild and paint the carved wooden altarpiece made by Giacomo del Maiano for the Confraternity of the Immaculate Conception at San Francesco Grande, Milan; the central panel was to show Our Lady with her Son and angels, in oil. The National Gallery names the notary as Antonio de' Capitani and gives a fee of 800 lire.

claims.value: The Louvre panel is the first version, the one painted under the 1483 contract
claims.statement: That the Louvre picture is the panel produced under the 1483 contract and later removed from the confraternity (sold or otherwise diverted) is the prevailing scholarly reconstruction; the National Gallery describes the London panel as a replacement for it. No document names the Louvre panel.
